color.note: Dark is the first theme: the product UI, the landing page and the Atlas are night-ground surfaces. Light (paper) serves docs, print and prefers-color-scheme: light. Every value is explicit: no token aliases another, so a consumer that reads values gets the colour, never a {name}. Every text pair, mark and border pair is computed by the README's Contrast script in both themes.

tokens.name: ground
tokens.usage: Page background: night in the product UI, star-chart paper in docs and print. Every text token below is checked on it.

tokens.name: ground-alt
tokens.usage: Cards, memory cards, review cards, menus, inputs and diagram plates: one step above ground. Elevation is this step, not a shadow. Paper uses a warm off-white, never pure white.

tokens.name: panel
tokens.usage: Wells, code blocks, table row hover, the selected tree node.

tokens.name: rule
tokens.usage: 1px hairlines: card borders, table header rule. Decorative separation only; never the only edge of a control.

tokens.name: rule-soft
tokens.usage: Table row separators, header and footer rules, chart gridlines.

tokens.name: control-border
tokens.usage: The 1px border of inputs, secondary buttons and the dropdown trigger. Pairs in the README's Contrast section.4.11 asks 3:1).

tokens.name: line
tokens.usage: The kit's leader-line colour: plate ticks and construction lines in illustration only. In light it is 2.5:1, so never text, never an arrow that carries meaning (use edge).

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Body copy, headings, claim text, table cells. On ground, ground-alt and panel. Pairs in the README's Contrast section.

tokens.name: ink-dim
tokens.usage: Ledes, secondary copy, the author and workspace line of a card. On ground, ground-alt and panel. Pairs in the README's Contrast section.

tokens.name: ink-faint
tokens.usage: Labels, table headers, axis text. On ground, ground-alt and panel: 4.5:1 or more in both themes (see Contrast); never below 12px. Trust-critical lines (author, reviewer) use ink-dim.

tokens.name: edge
tokens.usage: Arrows and connectors that carry meaning in functional graphics (lifecycle, gate, pipeline, tree). Pairs in the README's Contrast section.

tokens.name: star
tokens.usage: Warm, the foundation: the active tab underline, step numbers, star text, the primary button's border. As text on ground, ground-alt and panel; pairs in the README's Contrast section.

tokens.name: star-fill
tokens.usage: The primary button's fill and the mark's star in graphics, with a 1px star border so its edge reads on paper. One primary per view, on ground or ground-alt, never on panel.

tokens.name: on-star
tokens.usage: Text on a star-fill (the primary button label). Pair in the README's Contrast section.

tokens.name: ice
tokens.usage: Cool, the lab: links, structure, selection, the orbit in graphics. Light is the kit's steel. As text on ground, ground-alt and panel. Pairs in the README's Contrast section.

tokens.name: focus
tokens.usage: Keyboard focus: a solid 2px outline at 2px offset on every control; on a filled button (star-fill, error) the 2px offset leaves a gap in the ground colour, so the ring is measured against ground and ground-alt, never against the fill. Pairs in the README's Contrast section.

tokens.name: held
tokens.usage: State held: written, waiting for an identity that did not write it. Chip word and open-ring glyph; text on ground, ground-alt, panel and held-soft. Also the colour of a pending ontology edge. Never an error.

tokens.name: promoted
tokens.usage: State promoted: approved by someone other than its author, readable, the tip of its claim. Solid-disc glyph; text on ground, ground-alt, panel and promoted-soft.

tokens.name: superseded
tokens.usage: State superseded: still promoted, no longer the tip; a newer version replaced it. Half-disc glyph; text on ground, ground-alt, panel and superseded-soft.

tokens.name: retired
tokens.usage: State retired: withdrawn by an approved retirement, kept on record. Slashed-ring glyph and a dashed chip border tell it from superseded; one step quieter than superseded; text on ground, ground-alt, panel and retired-soft.

tokens.name: rejected
tokens.usage: State rejected (and demoted): a reviewer refused it; the content is kept. Square glyph, the only square. Red means refusal or failure, nothing else.

tokens.name: in-progress
tokens.usage: A workspace in progress: its agents recall each other's memories before review. Dotted-ring glyph on the workspace; text on ground, ground-alt, panel and in-progress-soft.

tokens.name: unreviewed
tokens.usage: A held memory served before review inside an in-progress workspace. Same value as in-progress, written out (no alias): change the two together. The glyph (the held ring with a centre dot) and the word tell it from the dotted in-progress ring.

tokens.name: stale
tokens.usage: Marker stale: the anchor's source changed or vanished since promotion. Triangle glyph; text on ground, ground-alt, panel and stale-soft. A marker beside a state, never a state.

tokens.name: self-signed
tokens.usage: Marker self-signed: a version its own author approved, admitted only where a development workspace's tenant policy permits it; readable only inside that workspace, never promoted beyond it. Loop glyph; text on ground, ground-alt, panel and self-signed-soft. A marker beside promoted, never a state.

tokens.name: error
tokens.usage: Failure: error banners, the error code, an invalid field, the stop glyph on a refused path. Same value as rejected, written out (no alias): change the two together. Amber is never an error.

tokens.name: on-error
tokens.usage: Text on a solid error fill (a destructive confirm button). Pair in the README's Contrast section.

tokens.name: held-soft
tokens.usage: The held chip's tint (14% dark, 10% light). Fill only; the chip's word is held on it.

tokens.name: promoted-soft
tokens.usage: The promoted chip's tint (14% dark, 10% light). Fill only; the chip's word is promoted on it.

tokens.name: superseded-soft
tokens.usage: The superseded chip's tint (16% dark, 10% light). Fill only; the chip's word is superseded on it.

tokens.name: retired-soft
tokens.usage: The retired chip's tint (16% dark, 10% light). Fill only; the chip's word is retired on it.

tokens.name: rejected-soft
tokens.usage: The rejected chip's tint (14% dark, 10% light). Fill only; the chip's word is rejected on it.

tokens.name: in-progress-soft
tokens.usage: The in-progress chip's tint (16% dark, 10% light). Fill only; the chip's word is in-progress on it.

tokens.name: stale-soft
tokens.usage: The stale chip's tint (14% dark, 10% light). Fill only; the chip's word is stale on it.

tokens.name: self-signed-soft
tokens.usage: The self-signed marker's tint. Fill only.

tokens.name: chart-1
tokens.usage: Series 1 (blue), in this fixed order, never cycled. Marks: 3:1 or more on ground, ground-alt and panel; also 4.5:1 there, so a value printed beside its mark may take it, though labels and legends stay in ink. Checked by the dataviz validator (lightness band, chroma, CVD and normal-vision separation of adjacent slots) on ground in both themes.

tokens.name: chart-2
tokens.usage: Series 2 (vermillion), in this fixed order, never cycled. Marks: 3:1 or more on ground, ground-alt and panel; also 4.5:1 there, so a value printed beside its mark may take it, though labels and legends stay in ink. Checked by the dataviz validator (lightness band, chroma, CVD and normal-vision separation of adjacent slots) on ground in both themes. Never beside state chips: it sits close to rejected and held.

Checked by the dataviz validator (lightness band, chroma, CVD and normal-vision separation of adjacent slots) on ground in both themes.

tokens.usage: Series 4 (amber), in this fixed order, never cycled. Marks: 3:1 or more on ground, ground-alt and panel; also 4.5:1 there, so a value printed beside its mark may take it, though labels and legends stay in ink. Checked by the dataviz validator (lightness band, chroma, CVD and normal-vision separation of adjacent slots) on ground in both themes.

tokens.name: chart-5
tokens.usage: Series 5 (magenta), in this fixed order, never cycled. Marks: 3:1 or more on ground, ground-alt and panel; also 4.5:1 there, so a value printed beside its mark may take it, though labels and legends stay in ink. Checked by the dataviz validator (lightness band, chroma, CVD and normal-vision separation of adjacent slots) on ground in both themes.

tokens.usage: Series 6 (violet), in this fixed order, never cycled. Checked by the dataviz validator (lightness band, chroma, CVD and normal-vision separation of adjacent slots) on ground in both themes.

families.mono: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace

groups.name: Display
groups.note: Newsreader 600, the wordmark's face. Titles on the landing page, docs home, empty states and this book. Never below 18px, never in controls.

styles.name: display-hero
styles.sample: Nothing joins until a second look.
styles.usage: The landing hero only; clamp down to 34px on narrow screens.

styles.name: display
styles.sample: Why a write is held until another identity reviews it

styles.name: display-sm
styles.usage: Empty-state headlines and section openers in docs.

groups.name: Text
groups.note: Inter for every UI word. Tabular figures (font-feature-settings: "tnum") for counts, versions and times.

styles.name: title
styles.usage: The one h1 of a product page.

styles.name: lede
styles.sample: A held memory is visible to its own agent until someone other than its author approves it.
styles.usage: The sentence under a title, in ink-dim; max 44em.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: Each gets its own verdict as your reviewer key, as if you had reviewed it alone.
styles.usage: Everything else: claim text, copy, form values.

styles.name: body-dense
styles.sample: Retries use exponential backoff capped at 30 s.

styles.name: caption
styles.usage: Descriptive secondary text: reviewer lines, ladder words, figure captions, diagram text descriptions; ink-dim.

groups.name: Mono
groups.note: JetBrains Mono for ids, states, paths, codes and labels. Ligatures off for ids.

styles.name: code
styles.usage: Commands, claim keys, anchors, error codes.

styles.name: meta
styles.usage: Ids, claim keys, anchors and match lines in mono, in ink-faint or ink-dim. Descriptive words (approved by, protected) use caption.

styles.name: state
styles.usage: The state chip's word, always lower case.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Field labels and table headers, upper case, ink-faint.

spacing.note: 4px base (space-0.5 is the one 2px step, for hairline offsets). Gutter space-4 on phones, space-6 on desktop. Every padding and gap in bundle.css and the previews is one of these.

tokens.name: space-0.5
tokens.usage: Hairline offsets only: chip vertical padding, the focus offset, a checkbox margin.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Glyph to word inside a chip; icon to label.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Between chips; inside compact controls; table cell vertical padding (dense).

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Between the lines of a card; label to field.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Card padding; phone gutter; between form fields.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Between cards; desktop gutter; diagram node gap.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Before an h2.

tokens.name: space-12
tokens.usage: Between page sections.

tokens.name: space-16
tokens.usage: Page foot; hero padding.

radius.note: Three radii replace the eight found (5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 999). Dots and state glyphs are circles (50%), which is a shape, not a radius.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: Inline code, checkboxes, the square of a rejected glyph, table-size tags.

tokens.name: radius-md
tokens.usage: Buttons, inputs, cards, panels, menus, toasts: one curve for every box.

tokens.name: radius-pill
tokens.usage: State chips, toggles, filter pills.

shadow.note: Borders over shadows: elevation is ground-alt on ground. One shadow, for what floats.

tokens.name: shadow-float
tokens.usage: Dropdown menus, toasts, popovers. Nothing at rest carries a shadow.

tokens.name: focus-gap
tokens.usage: Not elevation: the ground-coloured 2px gap between a filled button and its focus ring, so the ring never touches the fill.

size.note: Fixed sizes that are not spacing.

tokens.name: target-min
tokens.usage: The smallest pointer target (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.8): checkboxes' hit area, icon buttons, tree toggles, toast dismiss.

tokens.name: control-h
tokens.usage: Buttons, inputs and the dropdown trigger.

tokens.name: control-h-sm
tokens.usage: The compact button inside a toast or a table row; still above target-min.

tokens.name: check
tokens.usage: Checkbox box; with a 2px margin its hit area is target-min.

tokens.name: glyph
tokens.usage: A state glyph inside a sm chip, a table cell or a meta line. Never smaller: below 12px the ring patterns blur.

tokens.name: glyph-lg
tokens.usage: A state glyph inside a lg chip, a toast or an error banner.

tokens.name: glyph-xl
tokens.usage: The gate glyph heading an empty state.

tokens.name: bar-h
tokens.usage: The lifecycle mini-bar and the progress meter: a 100%-stacked bar of state segments with a space-0.5 ground gap between segments.

tokens.name: spark-w
tokens.usage: A sparkline's width (recall over 30 days, queue depth over 7 days).

tokens.name: spark-h
tokens.usage: A sparkline's height; the last value is printed beside it in ink.

tokens.name: tm-min-w
tokens.usage: A treemap region narrower than this, or lower than tm-min-h, shows its count only; its name moves to the tooltip and the table twin.

tokens.name: tm-min-h
tokens.usage: See tm-min-w: the height a region needs for its name and count on two lines.

tokens.name: stroke
tokens.usage: Edges and connectors in functional graphics; Lucide icons.

tokens.name: stroke-strong
tokens.usage: The refused path and the version rail of a supersession chain.

tokens.name: measure
tokens.usage: The longest line of a lede or claim text.

tokens.name: card-max
tokens.usage: Every card's and banner's max width: memory, review, proposal, toast, capability note, confirm panel.

tokens.name: tile-max
tokens.usage: Graphic tiles (Atlas, empty state) and the empty-state copy block.

tokens.name: menu-min
tokens.usage: Dropdown menu min width.

tokens.name: header-h
tokens.usage: The sticky header's height; html sets scroll-padding-top to it so focus is never hidden under the header (WCAG 2.4.11).

tokens.name: bp-card
tokens.usage: Container width below which a card's facts stack and a table row becomes a two-line card. Written as a literal in bundle.css's @container rules, which cannot read variables.

tokens.name: bp-chain
tokens.usage: Container width below which a supersession or lineage chain runs top to bottom.

tokens.name: bp-figure
tokens.usage: Container width below which a functional graphic swaps its wide SVG for the tall one, so no label renders under 12px.

tokens.name: wrap-app
tokens.usage: Product pages' content width.

tokens.name: rail-w
tokens.usage: The side rail beside a product page's content column (progress meter, sparklines, selection details): card-max + space-6 + rail-w is the inner width of wrap-app, so cards, toolbars and tables share one right edge. Below bp-rail the rail stacks above the content.

tokens.name: bp-rail
tokens.usage: Viewport width at which a product page gains its side rail. A media-query literal in bundle.css, equal to this token.

tokens.name: wrap-site
tokens.usage: Landing page content width.
